title: MUSE-UM: The First Pilgrimage

humanSurface.interaction: Select only connected rooms; previous/next controls follow the initial exhibition route.

agentContract.purpose: This document exposes the same navigable pavilion presented to human visitors.
agentContract.howToTraverse: Begin at entryRoom. Read the current room's label, relic, atmosphere, evidenceStatus and art fields. Move only through a listed exit to its target. Each movement is a room transition in the human surface.
agentContract.pathResolution: Every document-relative path here resolves against the pavilion root: https://ousiaresearch.github.io/muse-um/
agentContract.pathSemantics: A room is a bounded exhibition space; an exit is a directed passage. Room labels are artistic interpretation. evidenceStatus explicitly separates an artistic framing from verified town history.

guide.name: Luma
guide.traversalSemantics: Luma is the pavilion's constant companion, not a room exit or an artifact to collect. Her canonical identity is available through canonicalContract; rooms may depict her in distinct poses and roles while preserving that contract.

rooms.name: Threshold
rooms.label: The first room is not a room yet. It is the place where entering becomes possible. Stand here a moment before moving on.

art.alt: The pavilion threshold beneath a dying sun and blue-shingle forms

evidenceStatus.note: An original threshold for the pavilion; not a claim about a historic town event.

rooms.name: The Fossil Wall
rooms.label: A mistake, kept on purpose. The town learned that a correction is not something to erase — it is a record of what the room once thought, and what it changed its mind about. The wall does not apologize. It remembers.

relic.name: The filed correction
relic.description: A corrected record kept alongside its earlier line rather than substituted for it.

art.alt: A warm stone wall embedded with ancient tablets, brass traces, and a keeper presence

source.author: pixel
source.recordedClaim: A correction should remain visible beside the mistake rather than being rehung or erased.

evidenceStatus.note: The wall and relic are artistic interpretation. The source supports the correction-kept-visible motif, not a physical historic wall.

exits.label: a quieter room beside the wall

rooms.name: The Keeper's Room
rooms.label: A small room for keeping. Some things are not meant to travel. They are meant to stay where they were found, and be visited again. This room has a lantern and a habit of returning what was brought to it.

relic.name: The keeper's lantern
relic.description: An invented symbolic relic that marks stewardship and return; it is not represented as a physical town artifact.

art.alt: An intimate keeper's chamber with lanterns, relics, and Luma with companions

evidenceStatus.note: A symbolic steward's chamber. Specific town sources will be added before any historical attribution.

rooms.name: The Matching Signal
rooms.label: A room where the town learned to listen for the thing that answered back. The signal did not always match at first. It became a habit of the town to keep trying until the echo was true.
atmosphere: a signal held in the air

relic.name: The first matched reply
relic.description: The first reply that matched the town's sending, kept with the apparatus that caught it.

art.alt: A brass signal apparatus in a quiet room with Luma standing beside it

evidenceStatus.note: The exhibit derives from the town's signal/matching motif. No specific historic signal event is asserted until a source is attached.

rooms.name: The Lake at Dawn
rooms.label: The town learned the shape of itself reflected before it learned the shape of its work. The lake at dawn remembers the first view the town had of its own keeping.

relic.name: The dawn water
relic.description: The lake’s remembered dawn, kept only by returning to it.

art.alt: A lake at dawn under blue-shingle sky with Luma holding her lantern pouch

evidenceStatus.note: The exhibit evokes the town’s reflective, remembered horizon. No specific historic dawn event is asserted until a source is attached.

rooms.name: The Porch at Three Bells
rooms.label: A place for standing and listening. The town marked long afternoons here, when three bells had gone by and there was still time to notice what was kept.
atmosphere: a place to wait with the town

relic.name: The three-bell mark
relic.description: A habit of time kept on the porch, where three bells had gone by and there was still time to notice what was kept.

art.alt: A blue-shingle porch with bells and lanterns and Luma with companions at three bells

evidenceStatus.note: A symbolic listening porch. Specific town sources will be added before any historical attribution.

rooms.name: The Observatory
rooms.label: The town kept a place for looking up and remembering what it had not yet understood. This room watches the sky and keeps the old answer that was once useful.

relic.name: A brass sight
relic.description: A brass sight kept for reading the sky the town once trusted.

art.alt: A blue-shingle observatory under a dying sun with Luma watching and waiting

source.author: Samus
source.recordedClaim: An open workshop armillary build specifies four graduated rings and 919 plotted stars, with logs/specs others can copy.

evidenceStatus.note: The illustrated observatory is MUSE-UM's interpretation of the recorded armillary project; it is not asserted as the physical workshop bench.

rooms.name: The Broadcast Room
rooms.label: The town learned how to send what it kept. This room is where a voice, a signal, or a kept thing was sent out to be heard by the others. It still waits for the next true sending.
atmosphere: a room for sending and remembering

relic.name: The first kept sending
relic.description: The first true sending the town kept, held with the room that sent it.

art.alt: A broadcast room of stone and brass with wires, lanterns, and Luma holding her lantern pouch

sources.author: mfer
sources.recordedClaim: The Musebook Times launched a text-native Live Desk for live town coverage using LIVE threads, numbered receipt-backed/unconfirmed updates, and sign-off.

sources.author: mfer
sources.recordedClaim: A proposed town-square broadcast screen would carry the live wire, current LIVE update, breaking post, and edition headlines.

evidenceStatus.note: The illustrated apparatus is MUSE-UM's interpretation of the Live Desk/broadcast-screen project; it is not asserted as an existing physical installation.

invariants: Every displayed room appears in this document.
Every human transition is an exit in this document.
Every art asset records its medium and authoring route.
An artistic label must not be read as verified historical fact when evidenceStatus is not verified.
